## Context
Releases currently upload macOS artifacts named `HackDesktop-1.0-macOS.{dmg,zip}` even when the CLI tag is `v1.x.y`.

Root cause: `xcodegen generate` overwrites `apps/macos/App/Info.plist` and hardcodes `CFBundleShortVersionString=1.0` and `CFBundleVersion=1`, so the built app always reports `1.0`.

## Goals
- Ensure the built app version matches release version (`MARKETING_VERSION` / tag `v${version}`).
- Ensure uploaded artifact names include the real version (e.g. `HackDesktop-1.4.3-macOS.dmg`).
- Prefer a repo-level fix (xcodegen config) over CI-only patching.

## Notes
- Candidate fixes:
  - Update `apps/macos/project.yml` `targets.HackDesktop.info` to set `CFBundleShortVersionString` / `CFBundleVersion` via `properties`.
  - Or patch the generated `App/Info.plist` after `xcodegen generate` and before `xcodebuild` in `.github/workflows/release-macos-app.yml`.

## Links
- `.github/workflows/release-macos-app.yml`
- `apps/macos/project.yml`
- `apps/macos/App/Info.plist`

## Context
- `hack session` is currently tmux-only (`src/commands/session.ts`).
- The implementation and docs diverge:
  - `hack doctor` currently warns that `fzf` is needed for sessions, but the picker is now `@clack/prompts` (`src/commands/doctor.ts` vs `src/commands/session.ts`).
  - Agent-doc snippet claims an fzf picker + that `hack setup tmux` installs tmux, but `hack setup tmux` only edits tmux config and requires tmux already installed (`src/mcp/agent-docs.ts`, `src/commands/setup.ts`).
  - `docs/sessions.md` shows session names like `project:2`.
- tmux session names cannot safely contain `:` or `.` (tmux normalizes them to `_`), which causes collisions and breaks the current suffix scheme (`${base}:${n}` / `${base}:${custom}`) and parsing assumptions.
- The daemon session API (`src/daemon/routes/sessions.ts`, documented in `docs/sessions.md` + `docs/gateway-api.md`) is hard-coded to tmux and should stay consistent with the CLI behavior.

## Goals
- Make sessions backend-pluggable (mux backend): `tmux` (default) and `zellij` (MVP).
- Fix session naming to be tmux-safe and collision-free:
  - Base: `<projectSlug>`
  - Extra sessions: `<projectSlug>--2`, `<projectSlug>--3`, ...
  - Custom: `hack session start <project> --name agent-1` => `<projectSlug>--agent-1`
- Define and document behavior when the configured backend is missing:
  - `auto` picks the first available backend
  - explicit `tmux`/`zellij` errors with actionable install hints
  - `none` disables sessions with clear messaging
- Align docs, `hack doctor`, and agent-doc snippets with the real implementation.

## Notes
- Introduce a `MuxBackend` interface shared by:
  - CLI `hack session` commands
  - daemon `/v1/sessions` routes (so desktop/gateway control works across backends)
- tmux adapter fixes:
  - stop generating names containing `:` or `.`
  - use a non-conflicting delimiter for `tmux list-sessions -F` output (e.g. `\t`), avoid `split(":")`
- zellij adapter MVP scope:
  - support `list`, `start`, `attach`, `stop`, `exec`
  - for `panes/capture/tail`, return a clear "not supported by zellij backend" error (documented)
- Config:
  - key: `sessions.mux` = `auto|tmux|zellij|none` (global default, project override allowed)
  - env override: `HACK_SESSIONS_MUX`
  - document `hack config set --global sessions.mux zellij`
- Update daemon session name validation to match the new naming rules (and avoid accepting names tmux will normalize).
- Tests:
  - unit tests for next-session name generation
  - unit tests for tmux list parsing and project association via session cwd/path

## Links
- `src/commands/session.ts`
- `src/commands/doctor.ts`
- `src/commands/setup.ts`
- `src/daemon/routes/sessions.ts`
- `src/mcp/agent-docs.ts`
- `docs/sessions.md`
- `docs/gateway-api.md`
payload.title: Sessions: mux backends (tmux default, zellij MVP) + fix tmux naming collisions

## Context
- We want “project meta” surfaced for DX and for the desktop app: git repo/branch/sha/dirty, worktrees, active sessions, branch instances, and service/runtime info.
- Today, `hack projects` + daemon `/v1/projects` are mostly compose-runtime oriented:
  - `src/lib/project-views.ts` includes runtime status, compose-defined services, service hosts, extensions.
  - daemon `/v1/projects` is backed by `src/daemon/runtime-cache.ts` and only knows about Docker/compose runtime (`src/lib/runtime-projects.ts`).
- Branch instances exist (compose project prefix `base--branch`) and branch alias metadata exists (`.hack/hack.branches.json` via `src/lib/branches.ts`), but there’s no unified “meta” view.

## Goals
- Add an optional meta layer per project:
  - git: repo present, HEAD sha, branch, dirty, upstream (best-effort)
  - worktrees: list from `git worktree list --porcelain`
  - sessions: sessions for repoRoot (from mux backend; associate by session cwd/path), including backend + attached
  - hack branch aliases: `.hack/hack.branches.json` (aliases + last_used_at)
  - branch instances: summarize current `branch_runtime` plus runtime status per branch instance
- Expose meta via:
  - CLI: `hack projects --json --meta` (default output unchanged)
  - daemon: `/v1/projects?include_meta=true` (backward compatible)

## Notes
- Performance: meta collection must be opt-in and fast; avoid git/mux probes unless requested.
- Implement focused probes/helpers:
  - `git`: safe `git` command wrappers + porcelain parsing
  - `sessions`: reuse mux adapter from Sessions ticket
  - `branches`: reuse `src/lib/branches.ts` (parse `.hack/hack.branches.json` if present)
- Prefer putting meta under a single `meta` key in serialized output to avoid breaking consumers.
- Tests:
  - worktree porcelain parsing
  - session-to-project association (path matching)
  - JSON shape stability (no-meta path matches current payloads)

## Links
- `src/lib/project-views.ts`
- `src/commands/projects.ts`
- `src/daemon/server.ts` (`/v1/projects`)
- `src/daemon/runtime-cache.ts`
- `src/lib/runtime-projects.ts`
- `src/lib/projects-registry.ts`
- `src/lib/branches.ts`
payload.title: Projects: richer project metadata (git/worktrees/sessions/branch instances) for CLI + daemon

payload.body:
## Context
- We want to be able to see (and edit) effective env per project/service, especially in the desktop app:
  - show which env is applied to each service
  - update values in place
  - have changes persist (likely via `.env` and/or secrets store)
- hack currently has:
  - `.hack/.internal/compose.override.yml` generation for DNS/TLS/extra_hosts (`src/commands/project.ts`)
  - `hack secrets` backed by OS keychain (`Bun.secrets`) but not wired into compose/service env resolution (`src/commands/secrets.ts`)
- There is no structured, shareable “env contract” for a project (required vars, per-service scoping, provenance).

## Goals
- Introduce a committed “env contract” file (no values) in `.hack/`, e.g. `.hack/hack.env.json`:
  - declare vars, per-service scope, required vs optional, and source (`plain_env` vs `keychain`)
- Add `hack env` command group (design for desktop + scripting):
  - `hack env list` (show contract + resolution state; secrets masked by default)
  - `hack env set KEY=VALUE` (writes non-secret values to `.hack/.env`)
  - `hack env set --secret KEY` (stores in keychain; does not write secret value to disk)
  - `hack env unset KEY` (remove from `.hack/.env` and/or keychain)
- Wire env resolution into runtime operations:
  - `hack up`, `hack restart`, `hack run` should inject required env into containers
  - do not write secret values into repo-tracked files
- Make it possible for the desktop app to read env status and update it safely:
  - add daemon endpoint(s) for reading resolution state (masked)
  - gated write endpoint(s) when gateway allowWrites is enabled

## Notes
- Compose injection approach:
  - keep `.hack/.env` for non-secret values (gitignored by default in most repos; ensure `hack init` adds `.hack/.env` ignore entry explicitly)
  - for secrets: resolve from keychain at runtime and pass via process env when invoking `docker compose`
  - generate a `.hack/.internal/compose.env.override.yml` that adds `${KEY}` to `services.<svc>.environment` based on the contract (placeholders only, no secret values)
- Keychain namespacing:
  - keep `Bun.secrets` but namespace names by project id or slug so secrets don’t collide across projects
- Validation:
  - on `hack up`/`hack run`, if required keys are missing, prompt in interactive mode; error in non-interactive mode
- Future (explicitly out-of-scope for this ticket’s MVP unless we split work):
  - encrypted, git-synced secret vault (age/sops-style) with local private key and shareable public keys

## Links
- `src/commands/secrets.ts`
- `src/commands/project.ts` (internal override generation)
- `src/lib/env.ts` (dotenv parsing helpers)
- `src/daemon/server.ts` (add endpoints for env views/updates)
payload.title: Env & secrets: env contract + per-service resolution + keychain integration + daemon-friendly views

payload.body:
## Context
- Many projects need host-side setup every time before `hack up`: auth steps (e.g. `aws sso login`), starting a local proxy/tunnel, etc.
- Today hack manages docker-compose services, but not “adjacent” host processes that must be started/stopped alongside a project.
- We need this to feel one-click in the desktop app and work well with sessions (tmux today; future mux backends).

## Goals
- Add project-scoped lifecycle hooks so `hack up` can run prerequisite commands and start long-running host processes, and `hack down` can tear them down.
- Support per-branch isolation (so branch instances don’t fight over ports/process names) where feasible.
- Make status observable: show what’s running, where it’s running, and recent logs.

## Proposed Design
- Config additions (project config):
  - `lifecycle.hooks`: ordered, short-lived commands with phases:
    - `preUp`, `postUp`, `preDown`, `postDown`
  - `lifecycle.processes`: long-running commands that hack can start/stop, with:
    - `name` (stable key)
    - `command` + `args`
    - `cwd` (default repoRoot)
    - `env` (inline overrides; reference env/secrets system)
    - `ports` (optional for conflict checks)
    - `branchScope`: `shared|per_branch` (default `per_branch`)
    - `stop`: `signal|command` (SIGINT/SIGTERM) + optional stop command

## Runtime Behavior
- `hack up`:
  - run `preUp` hooks (fail fast, actionable errors)
  - ensure session/mux context exists (if configured) so long-running processes have a home
  - start `lifecycle.processes` (idempotent: if already running, reuse)
  - run compose/kube backend up
  - run `postUp` hooks
- `hack down`:
  - run `preDown`
  - bring runtime down
  - stop managed processes (respect `branchScope`)
  - run `postDown`

## Implementation Notes
- Prefer to run long-running processes inside the mux backend session (tmux default), as dedicated windows/panes named after the process.
- If mux backend is unavailable, fall back to daemon-managed processes (or explicit error if not supported yet, depending on chosen MVP).
- Track process state in `.hack/.internal/` (pid files, metadata) and ensure it is gitignored.
- Provide `hack lifecycle status` / `hack processes status` for the desktop UI and troubleshooting.

## Edge Cases
- Hooks that require interactive browser login (`aws sso login`) should still work; provide clear prompts and allow continuing after auth completes.
- Ensure teardown is best-effort and safe: don’t kill unrelated processes; require pid tracking and/or marker files.
- Port conflicts when multiple branches are up: support templated ports (e.g. base + branch hash) or require `shared` scope explicitly.

## Tests
- Hook ordering and failure behavior
- Process idempotency (start twice => one process)
- Teardown correctness (down stops only managed process)
- Branch scoping rules

## Links
- `src/commands/project.ts` (up/down wiring)
- `src/commands/session.ts` (if mux integration is used)
- `.hack/.internal/compose.override.yml` pattern (internal state location)
payload.title: Project lifecycle hooks: startup scripts + managed host processes (aws sso login, local proxies) with teardown

payload.body:
## Context
- hack is currently Docker/compose-first (`src/backends/runtime-backend.ts`, `src/lib/runtime-projects.ts`, daemon cache + docker events).
- Some projects are Kubernetes-native; we want a world where hack can manage local kube (minikube/kind) similarly to compose projects.
- Branch instances are already a core hack concept (compose naming `base--branch`); kube needs an analogous isolation story.

## Goals
- Add a runtime backend abstraction that supports `compose` (existing) and `kubernetes` (new).
- Project config:
  - `runtime.kind` = `compose|kubernetes` (default `compose`)
  - `kubernetes.*` config (context, namespace base, deploy mode/path, service selectors)
- Implement kube equivalents for:
  - `hack up`, `hack down`, `hack ps`, `hack logs`, `hack run`, `hack open` (MVP semantics documented)
- Branch instances:
  - map `--branch <slug>` to isolated namespaces/releases like `<namespaceBase>--<branchSlug>`

## Notes
- Backend interface work should build on `src/backends/runtime-backend.ts` (expand beyond compose-only).
- Kube deploy modes (pick 1 for MVP, allow future extension):
  - raw manifests (`kubectl apply -f <path>`)
  - kustomize (`kubectl apply -k <path>`)
  - helm (`helm upgrade --install ...`)
- `hack open` for kube MVP:
  - prefer `dev_host` + ingress if configured
  - otherwise support port-forward (explicit config for service/port)
- Daemon/runtime-cache:
  - MVP can be CLI-only; follow-up work adds kube-aware `/v1/projects` runtime discovery and watch/polling.

## Links
- `src/backends/runtime-backend.ts`
- `src/commands/project.ts` (up/down/ps/run wiring today)
- `src/lib/runtime-projects.ts`
- `src/daemon/runtime-cache.ts`
payload.title: Runtime: Kubernetes backend (minikube/kind) alongside docker compose

## Context
